themes.light: :root[data-theme="light"] remaps ground, mat, paper, field, graph field and shadows; accents and labels unchanged.
themes.paperRemap: .panel, .settings-pop, .info-pop, .help-pop, .tour-card remap --text/--text-2/--muted/--line/--line-strong/--hover/--focus to ink and paper tokens.

knownDefects: Captured pieces in player bars are Unicode chess glyphs with -webkit-text-stroke; replacing them with an SVG piece set awaits the owner's licence decision.
Close buttons render a text '×', the labels help button a text '?', and info triggers a text 'i' instead of SVG icons.
The mat ships as #1c3627 (direction contract said #1B3325); the build value is recorded.

narrative.overview:
The board every club player learned on, grown into the whole app. The page is the deep vinyl green of a roll-up tournament mat; the chessboard sits on a slightly lighter green mat with bold printed a–h / 1–8 coordinates in its margin and the eval strip tucked beside the ranks. Everything you read sits on buff scoresheet paper in dark ink, ruled with hairlines like a score pad. The review is a quiet, tactile evening at the club, not a dashboard.

Density is moderate and tool-like: the board takes the left of the viewport, a single 400px paper panel holds the coach, graph, move list and controls on the right. Colour is spent sparingly and by meaning. Green marks where you are (current move, active tab, play, toggles, progress); brass marks what you can do (the one primary action in view). The Chess.com move-label colours and glyphs are inherited unchanged because players read them by habit.

The world explicitly refuses the category default of grey-dark panels with a blue accent and letter avatars. There are no decorative gradients, no glows, and no avatars; a small filled disc in the piece colour stands in for each player.
keyCharacteristics: Vinyl-green ground, darker-green board mat, buff paper panels with ink text.
Two accent roles only: green for position/state, brass for action.
Bricolage Grotesque for headings, numerals, coordinates and clocks; Figtree for everything read or clicked.
Hairline rules (1px, low-alpha ink or cream) separate content; no cards inside cards.
Flat at rest: shadows only on things that float or lift (popovers, the board, square badges).
Light and dark appearances share the same green mat and paper; only the ground and paper tint shift.

rules.name: The Green-Is-Here, Brass-Is-Do Rule
rules.body: Green only ever marks the current position or an active state; brass only ever marks the primary action. If a control is neither, it is paper (`buff-paper-2`) or ghost.

rules.name: The One Brass Rule
rules.body: At most one brass button per view region (coach actions, import form, summary footer). Secondary actions are ghost or paper.

rules.name: The Fixed Labels Rule
rules.body: Move-label colours and glyphs are the Chess.com convention and are never re-themed, re-ordered or recoloured by appearance or board theme.

rules.name: The Paper Remap Rule
rules.body: Anything placed on a paper surface (panel, settings, info, help, tour card) inherits ink text, paper hairlines, paper hover and a green focus ring by remapping `--text`, `--muted`, `--line`, `--hover` and `--focus` on the surface. Never hand-set ink colours inside paper; join the remap list instead.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every number that changes as you step through a game (clocks, eval text, accuracy, ratings, label counts, move numbers, dates, progress) is set with tabular figures so columns never jitter.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Bricolage for things that are printed on the club equipment (headings, coordinates, clocks, big numerals); Figtree for everything you read in sentences or press. Don't set body copy or buttons in Bricolage.

rules.name: The Section Label Rule
rules.body: The uppercase tracked label is the only heading of a data group. It never sits above a display headline or a title as an eyebrow.

rules.name: The Mat Is Flat Rule
rules.body: The mat and the panel never take a drop shadow. Only the board, floating popovers, the square badge and the phone's pinned controls cast one.

dos: **Do** keep the board on the mat at the left and the single 400px paper panel at the right; on phones the board comes first in review and the import panel comes first on the start screen.
**Do** use `club-green` for the current move, the active option, play and checked toggles, and nothing else.
**Do** spend brass on one primary action per region (Retry, Find games, Start Review).
**Do** separate panel content with 1px hairlines (`paper-line`) instead of nested cards.
**Do** set every changing number with tabular figures.
**Do** put new floating paper surfaces on the paper remap list so they inherit ink text and the green focus ring.
**Do** keep move-label colours and glyphs exactly as the Chess.com convention defines them.
**Do** offer the other board themes (Green, Walnut, Slate, Ice) and both appearances as user choices; Club is the default board.
donts: **Don't** fall back to grey-dark panels with a blue accent, or letter avatars; a side disc in the piece colour identifies each player.
**Don't** add decorative gradients or glows. The only gradients in the system are functional: the skeleton shimmer and the radial legal-move dots on the board.
**Don't** give the mat or the panel a drop shadow; shadows belong to the board, popovers, the square badge and the phone's pinned controls.
**Don't** use brass for selection or "current" state, or green for a call to action.
**Don't** set buttons or body copy in Bricolage Grotesque.
**Don't** stack an uppercase section label above a headline as an eyebrow.
